stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Most speakers of American English believe they pronounce the t in “top” and the t in “water” ______ acoustic recordings show that the t in “water” is usually a rapid tap of the tongue, closer to a d than to the crisp burst of air heard in “top.” The tap is so brief, lasting only a few hundredths of a second, that many listeners never notice it.
explanation: Both sides of the blank are complete sentences. “Most speakers… believe they pronounce the t… identically” can stand alone, and so can “acoustic recordings show that…”. Two sentences need a strong break such as a semicolon, and “however” starts the second sentence because that is where the contrast with the speakers' belief begins. The semicolon goes before “however,” and a comma follows it.

A.why: You treated “however” like “but” and joined two complete sentences with commas alone. That is a comma splice. Unlike “but,” the word “however” can't link two sentences on its own.

C.why: You put no punctuation at all where the first sentence ends, so the two sentences run together. “However” needs a semicolon or period in front of it here.

D.why: You attached “however” to the wrong clause. Putting the semicolon after it makes “however” end the first sentence, which is the opening of the passage, so it has nothing earlier to contrast with. The contrast belongs to the recordings, so “however” has to start that clause.
